data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'sabazios', meaning 'the god Sabazius'. In ancient Greek religion, Sabazius was the god of the wild, a protector of shepherds, and a healer. In Christianity, the name Sabasio is given to a boy, symbolizing a savior or helper, who brings comfort and protection. The name Sabasio carries the meaning “Savior, Helper” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Sabasio usually hope their child will grow to embody savior, helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_latin.name: Sabasius
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Sabasius originates from the Greek tradition, associated with the worship of Dionysus. As Sabazios, it was an epithet for the god, emphasizing his role as a savior and protector. This name was incorporated into Latin and used within early Christian contexts to signify a guardian or preserver.
